blocks.text: IN-DEPENDANCE by IBASHO presents The Feminine Gaze , a group exhibition bringing together four distinctive voices in contemporary photography: Lisen Stibeck , Birgit Graschopf , Ingrid Dorner and Florence D’Elle .

As dreamers, artists and explorers, these visual poets propose a different way of seeing, without taking the male perspective as the default. More than an aesthetic, the feminine gaze is a shifting perspective that asks not simply what we see, but through whose eyes we are seeing.

In Un Conte , Belgian artist and self-taught author-photographer Florence D’Elle embraces the slowness and materiality of large-format photography and wet plate collodion to revisit a deeply personal story. Through self-portraits and images of her daughter, she explores the place of women within the symbolic world of fairy tales, drawing on a past that is silent and luminous, yet also marked by violence. Inspired by the magical universes of Jean Cocteau and Jane Campion, D’Elle creates an oneiric realm in which symbolic gestures and motifs open onto another reality. The imperfections inherent to the collodion process become an essential part of her visual language, lending the images an organic, sensual and timeless quality. For the exhibition, D’Elle will launch Opprinnelsen , a book resulting from her artist residency at Sunnhordland Museum on the island of Halsnøy, Norway.

Ingrid Dorner is a French, Munich-based artist known for her evocative, surrealist-inspired photographic artworks. In the exhibition, Dorner presents works from three series: Liminal , Zimmer 23 and Merveille . Each acts as a different step in the same movement – an interior space, a process of transformation and a reopening of possibility. Zimmer 23 is about the interior space. Here, the room becomes both a physical and psychological space: a place of intimacy, protection, confinement and suspended time. Liminal occupies the threshold. It is the unstable moment when something is no longer what it was but has not yet become something else. Here, time, chemistry and manipulation act directly upon the photographic material. Transformation is not only represented, but it also physically takes place within the image via the photographic process called mordançage. Merveille suggests a reopening. Not an erasure of what came before, nor a simple resolution, but the fragile return of movement, imagination, sensuality and possibility. Together, the three series form a passage towards the possibility of seeing and inhabiting the world differently. During the exhibition, Dorner will present her newly published book Liminal – La chimie du temps by Hopper&Fuchs.

Birgit Graschopf is a Vienna-based artist who creates mysterious, sometimes whimsically staged scenes that always place female figures at the centre, depicting inner worlds of the photographed characters. Referencing gestures from Romanticism and Surrealism, her visual language oscillates between an atmosphere of what’s familiar and intimate, as well as what’s foreign and uncanny. Often, Graschopf colours her black-and-white photographs partially by hand, which, together with the prior manual application of photo emulsion on sandpaper or concrete, adds a painterly aspect and significantly contributes to the distinctive character of the images. The result of this process is ever-present in her series titled Still/Silence (2022–2026).

Lisen Stibeck is a photographic artist from Sweden with a keen interest in teenage identity and the inner landscape of the psyche, working with dreams and archetypes, shaping her work into a form of magical realism. For The Feminine Gaze , Stibeck presents A Quiet Distance , a series situated in a state of transformation, between inner and outer worlds, between presence and disappearance. This project explores how the feminine gaze perceives change as a lived, intuitive, embodied experience rather than a defined event. The title refers to the space between what is seen and what is felt, suggesting a quiet awareness that precedes transformation. The works invite a slower gaze, one that listens rather than looks and senses rather than defines.
The exhibition opens with a vernissage on 31 October from 16:00–20:00 and will run until 20 December 2026. The four artists will be present for a meet & greet. For more information, visit
IN-DEPENDANCE by IBASHO Waalsekaai 59 2000 Antwerp, Belgium www.in-dependancegallery.com
